Summary

TL;DR / In plain terms

Key concepts to understand

  • CE loss (bps/yr). The difference in U = expected return − (γ/2) × variance between two portfolios, times 252 × 10,000. This is the guaranteed annual return an investor gives up by holding the worse one.
  • Discretization, learning and total gap. The grid's best portfolio loses the discretization gap to the continuous optimum; the agent's choice loses the learning gap to the grid's best; the total gap is their sum.
  • Settled. Post-hoc: the first checkpoint after which the final portfolio is greedy at every checkpoint. The pre-registered rule (final action held ≥ K episodes) is reported beside it.
  • Family. Experiments with the same γ and grid. Comparisons line up entries of the same family across runs, so the table shows what else changed.

    6

    Notes, caveats and definitions

      Definitions of every measure
      • Learning gap: CE loss of the seed's final greedy portfolio against the best portfolio on its grid, from μ and Σ exactly.
      • Total gap: CE loss of that portfolio against the continuous long-only optimum.
      • Settled (post hoc): first log checkpoint from which the final portfolio is greedy at every later checkpoint.
      • Primary rule (pre-registered): the final greedy action held for at least K episodes through the end of training; the count includes the K window.
      • First hold ≥ K: first time any action stayed greedy for K episodes.
      • |ΔQ| rule: largest change in any Q-value stays below the tolerance in every full log window from then on.
      • Near-optimal (checkpoints): greedy portfolio within the near-optimal line at every later checkpoint. Every episode: the same, counting brief switches between checkpoints.
      • Average regret: expected CE loss of the portfolios actually played, averaged over all training episodes.
      • Tries to separate the top two: 8 sd² / gap², the tries of each before the two best grid portfolios differ by two standard errors, using the exact reward SD for that B.
